Fc.bar_b_note: B's panel is legible and on-direction (blue-grey, gold ingredients), but the dark, murky purple-rain world behind it has none of Palworld's saturated daylight or Valheim's atmospheric grade.

Up.bar_b_note: A clean, appealing stylised villager with clear face, eyes and earthy meadow palette carries it to Palworld NPC finish, though the neutral stage shows nothing of world light.

Pr.bar_b_note: A lone thin panel beside a flat-shaded low-poly boulder under flat noon light sinks it next to Palworld's dense, lived-in bases.

Fl.bar_b_note: B's scaled, naturalistic blue lizard nears the owner bar, but neither side shows the rim-lit material finish and A's flat cartoon shading, floating faint-mid and grey flipped belly sink it.

Kx.bar_b_note: The bright meadow light is decent, but speakers are tiny in the distance (Kell) or walled off by giant creature bodies (Corin, Captain Halder), so staging sinks it.

Rw.bar_b_note: A clear, on-direction blue-grey panel with gold/orange need counts and teal selection reads at shipping-game UI finish, held back only by small list sub-text.

Hx.bar_b_note: The naturalistic Galecrest is good, but the glide frame is a flat featureless green plain under haze and the landed bird keeps its raised-wing glide pose.

Sl.bar_b_note: The village-and-lake backdrop is pleasant, but the low camera buries the lower half in dark close grass and the creatures are small, so subjects lack Palworld's readable hero presence.

Lg.bar_b_note: The menu frame is on-direction, but the map itself is a flat green disc with road lines over grey fog, without the painted terrain a shipping game's map carries.

Ry.bar_b_note: Naturalistic fur-and-bristle creatures in warm sunlit grass with real dust impacts read close to Palworld fights, though the tell still lives in HUD text.

Uv.bar_b_note: A dark brown rock wall fills the Foreman frame and a black slab plus the player's back hide Garrick entirely, so neither frame stages the speaker in readable meadow light.

top_changes.change: Dialogue camera framing: place the camera so the named speaker is mid-frame and lit, with collision pull-in/fade for rocks and large creatures (Kx, Uv) and a closer shot for distant speakers.

Build the homestead wall as a thick timber frame with a cap, a distinct stone footing and a mid-value textured wattle/plaster infill (keep A's direction, not B's blown-out panel), and replace the flat-shaded boulder next to it.
Add a perch/folded-wing landed pose and a banked glide pose for flyers, and give the creature faint poses grounded contact (no floating faint-mid, no untextured flipped underside).
